reasons: Classification is correct: the cited audit clause (p0073) contains no frequency limit at all, which fails the fallback (once per year) and falls into the rule's walk-away zone (unlimited audits), so 'deviation' is justified even though cost allocation (Licensor unless >5% discrepancy), independent mutually-selected auditor, and absence of system access already meet or beat the preferred position.

Redline is minimal and correctly directed: it appends a once-per-twelve-months cap plus business-hours and confidentiality conditions to the existing sentence without disturbing the terms that already favor us, and inserts no new obligations on Customer.

The failed 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is a phrasing variant — 'Licensor shall not request more than one (1) such audit in any twelve (12) month period' plainly imposes the required annual cap. The 0.681 changed-character ratio reflects an insertion into a short sentence rather than an unnecessary rewrite.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice and prefix; it states what changed and why, cites the playbook position, and correctly acknowledges the favorable existing terms. Treating the missing express 30-day advance notice as a noted lesser point rather than a separate flag is consistent with the classification guidance.
